# Whitespace, paragraph marks and inline pictures

Original controls are generated by `tools/inline_picture_whitespace_fixture.py`.
Each case has Before/After text and a middle paragraph with a 14.25pt original
red square followed by the tested character. The paragraph mark is either 9pt
or 20pt; the run uses Verdana 10pt. `text-only.docx` removes the drawings without
changing the character or mark. The reference application exported the PDFs;
`tools/inline_picture_whitespace_reference.py` records baselines and hashes.

The reference application treats the following as blank-line characters: ordinary space, tab, U+2002
en space, U+2003 em space, U+2005 four-per-em space, U+200B zero-width space,
U+3000 ideographic space and U+FEFF. These allow picture-only line metrics, and
without pictures the paragraph mark determines the natural line height even
when its font is smaller than the whitespace run's font.

NBSP, narrow NBSP, thin/hair/figure/punctuation spaces, other tested Unicode
spaces and U+2060 word joiner retain text metrics. Their paragraphs ignore an
oversized final paragraph mark, like ordinary letters. Inline pictures in these
lines retain the text descender. Unicode `trim()` does not express this rule:
it both removes characters the reference application counts and retains U+200B, which the reference application ignores.

The original Verdana controls also expose separate glyph fallback behavior:
The reference application uses Arial for several Unicode spaces, Segoe UI Historic for U+1680,
Cambria Math for U+205F and Segoe UI Symbol for U+2060. Those fallbacks affect
line metrics and are not reproduced by this whitespace correction. The original
captures are retained as evidence of that remaining gap. The `*-explicit.docx`
variants specify those observed fonts directly, isolating whitespace treatment
from fallback selection. No font mapping is added to production code.

The two explicit-face sources contain 92 paragraphs under test; browser checks
all 184 Before/After baselines within 0.15pt of the reference application. Unit classification checks
are independently derived from the native text-only mark-size sensitivity.
Round-trip coverage changes a space to NBSP, checks the increased reservation,
reopens the export, and undoes to every original package part.

Relevant standards: ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.29 (paragraph-mark properties),
17.3.1.33 (spacing), 17.3.1.39 (consumer-defined automatic vertical alignment)
and 20.4.2.8 (inline drawing). The character classification is measured reference
behavior, not a Unicode-wide whitespace equivalence required by OOXML.
